capabilities: Navigate File Explorer and Search results with Vim-style j/k/h/l/g/G key bindings
Open files in new tabs, vertical or horizontal splits, or in the background
Create, rename, clone and delete notes and folders from the keyboard
Toggle selection on nodes and open the context menu via key bindings
Disable individual keys that conflict with other plugins
disambiguation: Despite the generic name, it currently supports only the File Explorer and Search tool windows, not all sidebar panels.
extras: Installable via BRAT or manually from releases; destructive mappings (delete) are disabled by default; author warns it may break plugins that alter File Explorer behavior; the popup preview action is work-in-progress; no runtime dependencies.
intentEvidence: Changes(improvements) to the native app features
motivation: The author built it to fill the gap for users who rely on a keyboard-based workflow: "The goal of this plugin is to fill this gap for users who rely on a keyboard-based workflow."
problem: Obsidian's Vim mode works in the editor but not in sidebar tool windows like the File Explorer, forcing keyboard-based users to reach for the mouse.

relations.evidence: NERDTree - A tree explorer plugin for Vim.
Neo-tree - Neovim plugin to manage the file system and other tree. like structures.

summary: Vim-style keyboard navigation plugin for the native File Explorer, adding key bindings for moving, opening, creating and deleting files and folders.
